advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the link-guard test's `rebar explain` topic scan tolerate line-wrapped references (e.g. normalize whitespace with `re.sub(r"\s+", " ", text)` before matching) so line-broken pointers are still validated.
evidence: src/rebar/_guides/passing-code-review.md:10-11: `See also its sibling guide — run \`rebar explain` / `plan\` — for the *plan*-review gate` (topic on the next line; `explain ` is followed by a newline, so `(\S+)` cannot capture `plan`)

The test docstring promises 'any `rebar explain <topic>` the prose points at must name a real registered guide/criterion, so the reachable-pointer promise can't rot' — a line-wrapped pointer escapes the regex, weakening that guarantee.
advisory.finding: The link-guard test's `explain_topic = re.compile(r"rebar explain (\S+)")` will not match `rebar explain <topic>` references where the topic is wrapped onto the next physical line (e.g. passing-code-review.md lines 10-11 render `rebar explain\nplan`), so that reachable-pointer promise is not actually validated by the guard the test claims to enforce.
scenarios: A future edit renames/removes a guide referenced only via a line-wrapped `rebar explain` pointer; the guard would not catch the now-dangling pointer.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the exit-code (0/1/2, merge, disabled) and `--help` behavior claims in the commit-trailer guide match verify_commit.py, and consider a drift guard.
evidence: Guide text: "Exit `0` means a candidate id resolved (or the commit is a merge, or the gate is disabled); exit `1` means nothing resolved ...; exit `2` is an I/O / store error"
Guide text: "`rebar verify-commit-ticket --help` prints the accepted forms too."

test_verify_commit_ticket.py only asserts `vc.EXPECTED_FORMAT in guide` and test_plan_review_explain.py asserts the string `rebar verify-commit-ticket` is present — no assertion pins the exit-code/flag prose to source.
dropped.finding: The new packaged guide documents `rebar verify-commit-ticket` exit-code semantics (exit 0/1/2 and merge/disabled cases) and that `--help` prints accepted forms, but these behavior claims are hand-written prose with no drift-guard test — the added tests only pin EXPECTED_FORMAT and the literal string `rebar verify-commit-ticket`. If the command's exit codes or flags change, the guide silently goes stale.
scenarios: A future change alters verify-commit-ticket exit codes or removes/renames --help behavior; the packaged guide keeps asserting old semantics to repo-less clients.
